title: Minimal bisecting walls cut the longest axis and alternate at right angles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Minimal bisecting walls cut the longest axis and alternate at right angles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: For a rectangular cell to be divided equally by a partition of least area, the partition must cut across its longest axis, and in successive bisections each new partition must be at right angles to the one before.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: minimal bisecting partition of a rectangular cell \perp longest axis; successive partitions mutually \perp

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: From this we may draw the simple rule that, for a rectangular body or parallelopiped to be divided equally by means of a partition of minimal area, (1) the partition must cut across the longest axis of the figure; and (2) in the event of successive bisections, each partition must run at right angles to its immediate predecessor.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Minimal partitions in rectangular cells”. Scope: dividing cells of roughly rectangular shape, especially in plant tissues

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: minimal bisecting partition of a rectangular cell \perp longest axis; successive partitions mutually \perp

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.87

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim supplies exact geometric optima and angular predictions. Existing time-lapse plant datasets and standard segmentation make both the single-division and successive-division tests feasible.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure pre-division cell axes and successive wall orientations, comparing observed partitions with the equal-volume least-area plane and the predicted 90-degree alternation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Growth between divisions changes the longest axis.

Real cells depart from rectangular geometry.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The longest-axis rule and the right-angle alternation are explicit and apply to a recognizable subset of cells in public embryo and meristem volumes. Standard geometric measurements can confirm or refute them for that subset within weeks. Adequacy is limited to model plants rather than rectangular dividing cells in general, which is still enough for the rule as a biological regularity.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Among cells that are roughly rectangular and divide into near-equal daughters, test whether the new wall cuts the longest axis and whether the next wall is perpendicular to the previous one. That pattern would support the claim; equal divisions parallel to the long axis, or successive walls that are not orthogonal, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many cells in these volumes are not rectangular, so the test has to be restricted to the shape the rule assumes.

Tissue stress orients some divisions and can mimic or mask a pure longest-axis rule.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In dividing plant cells, the new wall cuts across the mother cell's longest axis (its normal is near-parallel to that axis), and when two successive divisions are both recent, the second wall is near-perpendicular to the first.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py range-extracts the five members per archive and, for each wall flagged new whose two flanking cells are >= 40 um^3 and whose bounding boxes do not touch the image border, takes the mother as the union of the two cells. The wall normal is the smallest principal axis of the midpoints of the voxel faces shared by the two cells (um coordinates); the mother's longest axis and elongation sqrt(lambda1/lambda2) come from the covariance of its voxel coordinates. theta is the folded angle between them. Part 2 searches for cells X sharing a new wall with both cells of another new wall Y1|Y2. As a control that was not pre-registered, 1000 randomly sampled walls per apex that are not flagged new are analysed identically. Secondary: the eLife table is read and fractions are computed by division type. Per-wall rows are written to data/part1.csv (regenerated, not committed); derived/part1_theta_histogram.csv has theta counts by wall kind and elongation bin.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Data: the same 8 Arabidopsis shoot-apex archives as thompson1917-ch08-02 (first 8 archive names, alphabetical, of Zenodo record 18711581). Sister pairs = the two cells separated by a wall in *_new_walls.tif; mother = their union; sisters >= 40 um^3, not touching the border. Part 1 (longest axis): theta = angle between the new wall's normal (smallest principal axis of the shared-interface voxel coordinates, in um) and the mother's longest principal axis (largest-variance axis of its voxel coordinates, in um); analysed for elongated mothers (sqrt(lambda1/lambda2) >= 1.2), all mothers reported too. Under random orientation the median theta is 60 deg. Part 1 passes if median theta <= 30 deg and >= 60% of elongated mothers have theta <= 30 deg. Part 2 (alternation): triples X, Y1, Y2 where Y1|Y2 is a new wall and Y1 and Y2 each also share a new wall with the same cell X (so Y divided after X|Y formed); phi = angle between the normals of wall Y1|Y2 and wall X|(Y1 u Y2), folded to [0, 90]. Part 2 passes if median phi >= 75 deg and >= 50% of triples have phi >= 70 deg. SUPPORTS if both parts pass.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Part 1 fails if median theta >= 50 deg; Part 2 fails if median phi <= 60 deg. REFUTES if both parts fail. MIXED for any other combination of pass/fail/neither. If Part 2 has fewer than 15 triples it is underpowered; the verdict is then Part 1's outcome (supports if it passes, refutes if it fails, mixed otherwise) with that limitation noted and confidence capped at 0.6. If Part 1 has fewer than 30 elongated mothers: inconclusive (underpowered). Secondary, reported but not used for the verdict: in eLife 79224 Figure 8 source data 2 (Laruelle et al. 2022, Arabidopsis embryo apical cells at 16C), the fraction of horizontally dividing cells whose longitudinal length exceeds their maximal radial length, and of longitudinally dividing cells whose longitudinal length is below it.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: median angle (deg) between the new wall's normal and the mother cell's longest principal axis, elongated mothers (axis ratio >= 1.2)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: IQR 20.3-58.4 deg; random-orientation median 59.8 deg; per-apex medians 27.2-52.9 deg across the 8 apices

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson derives the rule for an ideal rectangular parallelepiped bisected by a least-area plane: the plane is perpendicular to the longest edge, and successive bisections alternate at right angles. Real meristem cells are not rectangular, so 'longest axis' is the largest principal axis of the cell volume and the test is restricted to mothers that are measurably elongated (principal-axis ratio >= 1.2), where the axis is defined. Successive divisions are identified only where both walls are still flagged as recent in one snapshot, so Part 2 samples rapid successive divisions. Division orientation in the shoot apex is also influenced by tissue stress, which can mimic or mask the geometric rule; the test measures the outcome, not the cause.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Image processing data for manuscript: Control of plant organ growth through cell division orientation in inner tissues (Yates & Sablowski)

Laruelle et al. 2022, eLife 11:e79224, Figure 8 source data 2: longitudinal/radial length ratio measurements

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Part 1 is between the pre-registered pass and fail bands. New walls are better aligned with the mother's long axis than random planes (median 35.9 deg against 59.8 deg), but short of the 30 deg median and 60%-within-30-deg needed to pass (41%). Alignment increases with elongation: median 26.7 deg for mothers with axis ratio >= 2, and 42-48 deg for nearly isodiametric ones, as the rule predicts if 'longest axis' only matters when one is clearly longest.

Part 2 could not be tested. The dataset's new-wall detection pairs each cell with at most one sister (no cell lies on two new walls in any of the 8 apices), so no successive-division triples exist. Under the pre-registered rule the verdict is Part 1's outcome (mixed), with confidence capped at 0.6. The alternation half of the claim is untested.

A control that was not pre-registered weakens the support from Part 1. Walls not flagged as new, between arbitrary neighbouring cells, score better (median 26.5 deg, 59% within 30 deg) than new walls do. The union of any two adjacent cells is elongated across their shared wall, so this measure favours the rule by construction. New walls lining up less well than that geometric baseline suggests that the observed alignment is not evidence for a division rule beyond geometry.

Sister identification relies on the dataset's own new-wall filter, which flags 4,365 walls in the first apex (8,730 of 12,499 cells), more than a single recent round of division would give. It probably includes older walls, which this test cannot separate from recent ones.

The 'cell crosses image border' field in *_cell_data.csv is 0 for every cell, so border contact was judged from each cell's bounding box touching the image edge. Mothers whose sister volumes the segmentation already limits to >= 40 um^3 all pass the volume filter.

Secondary (eLife 79224, embryo apical cells at 16C, not part of the verdict): 136 of 140 longitudinal divisions are in cells whose radial length exceeds their longitudinal length, as the rule predicts. All 9 transverse divisions are also in such cells, against the rule. Nearly all these cells are radially longer (median ratio 0.73), so the table cannot show cells choosing their division by length.

Shoot-apex division orientation is also influenced by mechanical stress and growth direction, which this test does not separate from geometry.

preregistered_at is the time of the pre-registration commit (9e0ec83d); the committed pre-registration carried an estimated time (21:40Z) written before committing. Data were first fetched after that commit; criteria are unchanged.
